craft_notes: Sthāyin: wheel-course — the ahnika's ritual peak. Rows: seating, filling, sating, circling. Rejected: shortening — killed: completeness. Read aloud: processional.

lines: Midmost the master, ringed in veiling order — from master down to the last bound, hero, goddess by turns —
sit ringed or ranked. Then scent and smoke and blooms in turn adore.
The bowl beheld as Ever-bliss, brimmed with Her nectar-wine;
the tasting goddess praised as Śiva; by her the god-ring sated;
the triad — man, might, Śiva — one-natured, held in mind;
then in veil-descending order, release and relish first, within, without — sate;
then circling back again: so the whole round feeds the wheel.
l4.sanskrit_cite: tatra madhye guruḥ tadāvaraṇakrameṇa gurvādisamayyantaṃ vīraḥ śaktiḥ iti krameṇa ity evaṃ cakrasthityā vā paṅktisthityā vā āsīta tato gandhadhūpapuṣpādibhiḥ krameṇa pūjayet tataḥ pātraṃ sadāśivarūpaṃ dhyātvā śaktyamṛtadhyātena āsavena pūrayitvā tatra bhoktrīṃ śaktiṃ śivatayā pūjayitvā tayaiva devatācakratarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā naraśaktiśivātmakatritayamelakaṃ dhyātvā āvaraṇāvataraṇakrameṇa mokṣabhogaprādhānyaṃ bahir antaś ca tarpaṇaṃ kuryāt punaḥ pratisaṃcaraṇakrameṇa evaṃ pūrṇaṃ bhramaṇaṃ cakraṃ puṣṇāti
